title: Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy under Theodoric
summary: In March 493 CE, following a three-year siege of Ravenna, the Ostrogothic king Theodoric assassinated King Odoacer at a banquet and eliminated his followers, establishing the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy with the sanction of Constantinople. Governing from Ravenna and Rome until his death in 526, Theodoric maintained Roman administration, laws, and the Senate while Goths held military command. His reign brought decades of peace, religious tolerance, and urban restoration across the Italian peninsula.

uncertainty.note: Assassination of Odoacer on 15 March 493 at the palace banquet in Ravenna marked the definitive establishment of Theodoric's sole rule over Italy.

as_recorded.value: 15 Mar 493 CE King Odoacer is assassinated at a banquet in Ravenna, Italy by Theodoric the Great, inaugurating the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy... In the course of the year 493 Theodoric had become the unchallenged master of Italy
after Theoderic had entered Ravenna and killed Odoacer, the Goths... confirmed Theoderic as their king

where.modern_name: Ravenna, Emilia-Romagna, Italy (capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy)
where.historical_name: Ravenna, royal residence and capital, Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy

importance.justification: Established stable Germanic-Roman dual administration in Italy under Theodoric after decades of imperial collapse, preserving classical urban culture, legal traditions, and monuments.

related.because: The collapse of the Western Roman Empire created the power vacuum that allowed Odoacer and subsequently Theodoric to establish kingdoms in Italy.

sources.title: Excerpta Valesiana, Pars Posterior: The History of King Theodoric
sources.author: Anonymous (trans. J.C. Rolfe)

beats.caption: Theodoric assassinates King Odoacer during a banquet at Ravenna, ending the three-year siege and civil war.
Theodoric establishes the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy, inaugurating over three decades of political stability and civic restoration.

reviewer_note: Dating to 15 March 493 CE follows contemporary chroniclers recording the banquet of Ravenna ten days after Theodoric's entry into the city. Coordinates pinpoint Ravenna, Theodoric's royal capital and burial site.
